Note that plugging in $x=0$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{3x}-1}{x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[{e}^{3x}-1]^{′}}{[x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{3{e}^{3x}}{1} \\  & =3{e}^{3(0)} \\  & =3(1) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
